title: Four-seat 180 mph car
pipeline: carAcceptanceAsync (CAD body, tub, aero build-up, drawings)
brief: Design a car that weighs 2,500 lb, can go 180 mph, seats 4 people, and has a futuristic aerodynamic look.

topSpeed.basis: speed limiter set point (design choice, 295 km/h); without it, the lower of the drag-limited and gear-limited top speeds

disclaimers: Software screening only. Passing software checks is not physical validation; every result below still needs the physical tests listed.
Aerodynamics is a component drag build-up and 2D panel screening, not CFD or wind-tunnel data.
caveats: The kerb mass is a lower bound: 40 item(s) the parts' published masses exclude are not in it (see massBreakdown.excluded).

The top speed is a model output (model_output_unvalidated), not a measurement: Cd 0.19006044550065382 is computed (screening range): aero.drag-buildup centre of 0.107..0.338 (not CFD or wind tunnel), frontal area computed from BODY_SHELL (cad.body: projected area of the kernel solid onto the y-z plane), driveline efficiency 0.9 given.

The vehicle top speed (295.0 km/h, 183.3 mph) is the set point of an electronic speed limiter that is a design choice, not built or calibrated; the tyre check relies on its overshoot staying within the 5 km/h design allowance. Without it the model gives 361.1 km/h (224.4 mph, model_output_unvalidated).

The gear limit rests on an estimated redline (7500 rpm): estimated: Ford does not publish a redline for the Gen 4 / Gen 4X crate engines (product pages; the 2020 Mustang technical specification lists the GT's redline as N/A). 7,500 rpm is the Mustang GT tachometer redline since the 2018 (Gen 3) engine as reported from the gauge cluster; the low end is the 7,000 rpm redline of the 2015-2017 (Gen 2) engine reported in the same article.
REQ_mass passes on a lower-bound mass.
REQ_topSpeed passes on a model output (model_output_unvalidated), not a validated top speed: the limited speed (the 295 km/h set point) is reachable only if the unlimited model output holds.

Packaging is screening level: not checked for want of dimensions or design: bellhousing, SUSPENSION_FRONT, SUSPENSION_REAR, STEERING_RACK, EXHAUST, CONTROL_PACK, SEAT_3, SEAT_4, BRAKES_FRONT, BRAKES_REAR, structural tub, pedal box, dash, steering column, driveshaft, doors, suspension travel.

physicalTests: Cd and frontal area: Cd is an input or the centre of a screening drag build-up range (no CFD or wind-tunnel value); frontal area is given, from the CAD body (computed from the solid) or from an ellipsoid body (screening) (the top speed depends on it)
driveline efficiency is an input, not measured or computed from the gearbox and differential (the top speed depends on it)
the gear limit needs the gear ratios, final drive, tyre radius and a redline; the redline and the power available at that engine speed are inputs (vehicle.gearing) (the top speed depends on it)
tyre speed rating and load index against this speed and the axle loads (tire.speed-rating, tire.load-index) (the top speed depends on it)
high-speed stability and aero lift: no solver yet (the top speed depends on it)
cooling capacity for sustained full power: no solver yet (the top speed depends on it)
the electronic speed limiter is a design choice: its calibration, the accuracy of the road-speed signal it acts on and its overshoot are not verified (the top speed depends on it)
Weigh the built car: the kerb mass is a lower bound (items the published part masses exclude are listed below)
Torsion rig test of the tub: the stiffness is a frame/shell model, not a measurement
Coast-down or wind-tunnel test: Cd is a screening build-up range, not CFD or a wind tunnel
Occupant fit and egress with real people in a buck or prototype
